title: Christmas Light Show in the Park
headline: A pavilion stage, two mega trees and a crowd on the lawn.
summary: On December 5, 2025 our music-synchronized show lit a park pavilion in Chatham-Kent: the stage outlined in pixels with snowflakes in the gable, two mega trees with star toppers, singing-tree faces and candy canes, all sequenced to the soundtrack while families watched from the snowy lawn.
scope: Two pixel mega trees with star toppers
challenge: A park pavilion is built for a band, not a light show. The brief was to turn it into the centrepiece of a winter evening: readable from across a snowy lawn, paced to music, with every prop facing the crowd the way a stage set does.
approach: We traced the pavilion's gable and eave in pixels, ran pixel verticals up the porch columns and filled the gable with snowflakes. Two mega trees with star toppers flank the stage, with singing-tree faces and candy canes in front. Every element is sequenced to the soundtrack, from slow colour washes to full-tree beat hits, with searchlight beams pushing colour into the sky behind the roof.
outcome: Families filled the lawn in front of the stage and stayed to watch the show through the evening. The clips on this page are unedited phone footage from show night, with the audio removed.

title: Blenheim Rotary Club Christmas Parade
headline: A community parade, scored and synchronized.
summary: Ontario Light Shows designed and operated a music-synchronized, addressable LED installation for the Blenheim Rotary Club's annual Christmas Parade — turning a small-town parade into a regional draw with thousands of programmed pixels sequenced to the holiday soundtrack.
challenge: The Rotary Club wanted to transform their long-running community parade into a regional headline event — without sacrificing the small-town, family character that had made it a tradition. We had to deliver a production-quality music-synced light show on a parade route, in winter, on a community budget, and with zero downtime tolerance on show night.
approach: We built the entire show in-studio against the final audio mix the parade committee approved, pre-loaded sequences onto outdoor-rated controllers, and weather-sealed every connector to IP67. A wireless cue rig let our operator trigger transitions in time with the parade announcer. Pixels were mounted to a parade-stage rig that broke down into modular sections so the same install could be reused across multiple parade nights and stored compactly off-season.
outcome: The 2024 parade drew the largest crowd in the Rotary Club's recorded history, picked up local press coverage, and converted into year-over-year donations for the club. The pixel rig and show file are now an annual asset — we run software updates and add new sequences each year instead of starting from scratch. The Rotary's lead organizer has called the show "the single biggest reason new families are showing up," and the project has become a calling card for our experiential work across Southwestern Ontario.
testimonialQuote: Ontario Light Shows didn't just hang lights — they choreographed our whole parade. The crowd reaction was unbelievable. It changed what a small-town Christmas parade can be.
